story: Casey MacGill, a bandleader whose path ran through the Broadway musical Swing before Seattle, brought his Blue 4 Trio to Pickathon in 2003 and again in 2010 and 2012. The trio made three CDs, the last of them Barrelhouse, and toured Europe for swing dancers.

act: Danny Barnes and the Piano Throwers
intro: A banjo player with a shifting cast of bandmates.
story: Danny Barnes, the Bad Livers founder, brought one of his early shape-shifting ensembles, the Piano Throwers, to Pickathon in 2003. Later he was invited to direct a collection of players at the Northwest String Summit.
Dylan Thomas Vance played Pickathon in 2003.
El Son del Pueblo, a Latin roots group, played Pickathon in 2003.

Foghorn Stringband, which Sammy Lind and Caleb Klauder started in 2000, played Pickathon in 2003, the year a tour to Juneau, Alaska, introduced them to bassist Nadine Landry. She joined for good in 2008, and as Foghorn Trio they recorded Sud de la Louisiane in Eunice, Louisiana, in 2010.
sets: Fri Aug 22, 9 pm · Sat Aug 23, 7 pm

story: Jackstraw, the Portland bluegrass band, returned to Pickathon in 2003. Darrin Craig, Jon Neufeld, David Pugh and Jesse Withers met at Artichoke Music in 1997, and by 2001 they were making a three-week tour east toward the home of bluegrass.

intro: A Dublin-born button accordion player living in Portland.
story: Johnny B. Connolly, two years past his solo debut Bridgetown, played Pickathon in 2003, 2004 and 2008. Kevin Burke, the Bothy Band fiddler who lives in Portland, played on three tracks of that record, and Connolly later toured with Casey Neill and Lisa Ornstein.

The Kitchen Syncopators, a ragtime and jug band that Gill Landry and Woody Pines started in 1998, played Pickathon in 2003. They built a following in New Orleans, and by 2006 their Tractor Tavern shows in Seattle had inspired the Lowdown Ramblers to form.

intro: A Portland singer-songwriter and a folk collaborator.
story: Little Sue, who came to Portland in the 1990s with her band the Crackpots, and Lynn Conover, a fixture of the Portland folk circuit who has played in duos with her, were on the 2003 bill. Sue has sung harmony on more than 50 local releases.

intro: A Boulder bluesman who plays banjo.
story: Otis Taylor, who came back to music in 1995, won the Blues Music Award for best debut for White African, and played Pickathon in 2003, the year Truth Is Not Fiction came out on Telarc. DownBeat's critics named it the year's best blues album, and he won a Blues Music Award for banjo in 2009.

Retta and the Smart Fellas, the Western swing band of Retta Christie, played Pickathon in 2003. It was her first professional band, playing Elks and Legion halls along the coast around 1982, and in 2007 she was back on Portland's KBOO with a Western swing show.

The Roy Kay Trio, a Seattle rockabilly band led by Roy Konitzer, played Pickathon in 2003. It started in 2001, released Rock-A-Way Lonesome Moon in 2005, and by 2012 had played in ten countries and made five albums.

intro: A dark-toned San Francisco old-time band.
story: The Crooked Jades, Jeff Kazor's San Francisco old-time band, played Pickathon in 2003, 2005 and 2007.
Trashcan Joe, a jazz act, played Pickathon in 2003.
